(Clause 31) AWARD 1.
As per the facts of the present case, on 03.09.2017 at about 7.30 AM, the deceased Smt Amlesh Devi W/O Vijay Pal Singh, alongwith her husband, was standing at Mohan Nagar Chauraha, UP.
She was waiting for a bus to board for her native village.

As soon as a bus destination to native village of deceased came and deceased proceeded to board the bus, suddenly a bus bearing No. UP33AT2448 came from behind in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased forcefully.
As a result of impact of the offending bus, the deceased died on the spot.
The deceased was taken to District Govt Hospital, Ghaziabd U.P where her post mortem was conducted, on the same day.
The present claim application has been filed for compensation regarding death of Amlesh Devi.

2. Since the offending bus bearing no. UP33AT2448 was driven by Mukesh Kumar, hence he was impleaded as respondent no. 1.The offending vehicles pertains/owned by Sahibabd depot, Ghaziabad,U.P, hence ARM Sahibabad has been impleaded as respondent no. 2 in the present claim application.
By the present claim application, the petitioners are claiming a sum of Rs. 20,00,000/ (Rupees Twenty Lacs Only) from respondents as compensation.
3. Respondents have contested the present claim.
4. The Respondent no. 1 has not filed any reply/WS in support of his case.
5. The respondent No.2, UPSRTC, has filed its WS stating therein that no accident had taken place with the offending bus.
But police officials have forcibly took the bus to police station and lodged a false and fabricated case.
And also by implicated the bus of UPSRTC in the present case.

6. After completion of the proceedings, following issues were framed on 22.10.2018:

I have heard ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.2 None appeared on behalf of R.1 to argue the case finally.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.1: Whether Amlesh Devi sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt 03.09.2017 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle i.e. Bus bearing registration No. UP33AT2448 being driven by Respondent No.1 and ,
owned by Respondent No.2 UPSRTC3? .. OPP 9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove this issue petitioner No.1, husband of the deceased, examined himself as an eye witness.
PW1 has deposed that on 03.09.2017 at about 7.30 AM, he alongwith his wife Smt Amlesh Devi ( deceased) were standing at Mohan Nagar Chauraha, UP.
He has deposed that they are waiting for a bus to board for their native village.

As soon as a bus destination to their native village came and deceased proceeded to board the bus suddenly offending bus bearing No. UP33AT2448 came from behind in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased forcefully.
As a result of impact of the offending bus, the deceased died on the spot.
The deceased was taken to District Govt Hospital, Ghaziabd U.P where her post mortem was conducted, on the same day.

10. PW 1 has been duly crossexamined by the Insurance company but the testimony of this witness with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 could not be impeached.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/304A of IPC.
PW1 is also the complainant in the criminal case and the FIR was also registered on his statement.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a bus bearing No.UP33AT2448 being driven by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Smt Amlesh Devi W/O Vijay Pal Singh.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Smt Amlesh Devi died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Bus bearing No.UP33AT2448 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2:
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation,if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
12.
Petitioner no.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 to 4 are sons of victim ( deceased Smt Amlesh Devi ) as such LRs of victim.
They are entitled for compensation.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
PW 1 ,husband of the deceased has deposed that at the time of accident his wife was doing the work of Tailoring and Embroidery and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.
On the other hand, Ld Counsel for the Insurance company submits that there is no evidence qua proving the monthly income of the petitioner.

However Ld Counsel for the petitioner fairly admitted that he has not placed on record any document qua showing the income of petitioner and submits that income of the petitioner may be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act prevailing in U.P at the time of accident.

So this Tribunal, while assessing the income of deceased under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in U.P, has assessed the income of deceased for the computation of compensation under the head of unskilled labour as Rs.5750/ p.m.
14.

As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 10%.
15.

sentences.text: There are four L.Rs of deceased ie her husband and three sons, at the time of accident, so deceased was spending 1/4th of her income on her personal expenses.
Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.4,744/ (5750/ + 575/  1581/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 51 years old at the time of accident ( 01.01.1966, as per Aadhar Card )
A multiplier of 11 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 6,26,208/ (4,744/ x 12 x 11).
This amount of Rs. 6,26,208/ is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.

17. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioner no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses, Rs.17,000/ for loss of estate and Rs. 44,000/ each to the petitioners for loss of consortium making a total sum of Rs. 8,36,208/

Detail of the whole award amount is: i. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,26,208/ ii. Funeral expenses Rs. 17,000/ iii. Loss of Estate Rs. 17,000/ v. Loss of consortium (44,000/ each to Rs. 1,76,000/-
 the petitioners )
